title: Paradise
physical_identity: A night forest oasis with crashing waterfalls, crimson dew-wet grass and an eternally starlit sky, narrated in second person as a lure; guests lie in the soil with glistening bones.
scale_topology: Not stated; described as a forest basin. No measurements or structures given.
anomalies: voices whisper and a cacophony replaces thought
children in rows howling at the moon
lighting_sound: Starlit night with moonlight; waterfalls, whispering forest, cacophony, beautiful howling.
items_communities: a collective speaking as we in the lure text

entrances.method: Article says keep going; interviewee claims stretching a hole in his brain
entrances.quote: You know how to get there by now. Just keep going.

exits.method: No exit given; interviewee will not say how he left
exits.quote: You won’t have to worry about that.

signature_mechanic: A lovely night forest that coaxes the visitor to surrender and stay; the page withholds entrance and exit.
verticality: None stated; waterfalls are scenery only.
do_not: treat lure prose as a safe haven
treat the interview as article fact
conflicts_notes: Prose is second-person and deceptive; interview log is TESTIMONY. Survival class absent. Link list contains author-page navigation only.

key_quotes.quote: The crimson grass, wet with dew.
their bones glistening in the moonlight
You know how to get there by now. Just keep going.
You won’t have to worry about that.
You wouldn't want to leave anyway.
